title: Fix Web Audio API sound system (effects + background music)

requirements.summary: Fix the Web Audio API sound system to ensure all sound effects and background music play correctly, complying with browser autoplay policies and properly handling AudioContext lifecycle
acceptanceCriteria: Sound effects (piece placement, line clear, level up, game over) play audibly when the corresponding game events occur.
Background music starts looping after the first user interaction with the game and continues without interruption during gameplay.
No 'AudioContext was not allowed to start' browser console errors appear.
The mute toggle button silences all audio (effects and music) immediately and un-mutes them correctly on toggle.
AudioContext is not recreated on every mute/unmute cycle; the same context is reused throughout the session.
Sounds work correctly across all supported game modes (Classic, Time Attack, Endless, Challenge, Puzzle, Insanity, Mirror Mode, Gravity Shift, Combo Rush).

file_operations.description: Refactor the audio hook to defer AudioContext creation until first user interaction, implement proper suspend/resume logic on every interaction, ensure mute toggle uses suspend/resume instead of destroying the context, fix buffer caching and music looping to prevent interruptions, and handle autoplay policy compliance by listening for any user interaction (click, touch, keypress) before initializing audio playback.
Update the context wrapper to expose the refactored audio system from useTetrisAudio and ensure backward compatibility with existing consumers using the useTetrisAudio alias.

Review and fix all audio hook integration points to ensure play functions (playLandSound, playLineClearSound, playLevelUpSound, playGameOverSound) are correctly triggered on game events (piece placement, line clearing, leveling up, game over), and verify that all game modes properly fire these audio triggers.

Verify the mute toggle button correctly calls the audio context's suspend/resume functions and reflects the current mute state visually, ensuring immediate audio silencing without destroying the AudioContext.

Add a global user-interaction listener (click, touch, or keypress) that triggers AudioContext initialization and resume on the first interaction, ensuring compliance with browser autoplay policies and that background music starts correctly after user engagement.
